Variants.Content: The High Keep is located between the woodlands and hills in the western part of the North. It is a northern castle governed by the laws of Winterfell. It watched over neighboring logging lands, hunting grounds, and the road to the west coast; the strength of local lords came from land, timber, and grain stores that could last through the winter, not the pomp of the southern court.

Entry Highpoint Local families also rely on firewood, hunting grounds, peat, salt fish, and granaries to survive the long winter; if any road, well, spring, or wharf fails, the price will fall on them first.

Entry Highpoint They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the North; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hoof.

Entry Highpoint If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Those who repair the High Keep are familiar with shipbuilding wood, canvas, salt, fish catch, and stone to withstand the sea breeze. Those who comfort the families of the deceased are familiar with the old gods, weirwood trees, and the cemeteries left by their ancestors. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Highpoint They care about firewood, hunting grounds, peat, salt fish, and granaries that can survive the long winter. They also care about whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, they see whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
